definitions.explanation: To raise and train a wild animal until it becomes accustomed to humans. Can also be used figuratively to mean bringing someone under control.

examples.japanese: {野生|やせい}の{馬|うま}を{飼|か}い{慣|な}らす。
{飼|か}い{慣|な}らされた{鷹|たか}は{人|ひと}の{腕|うで}に{止|と}まる。
examples.english: A tamed hawk perches on a person's arm.

examples.japanese: {人間|にんげん}は{何千年|なんぜんねん}もかけて{狼|おおかみ}を{飼|か}い{慣|な}らし、{犬|いぬ}にしたと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that humans tamed wolves over thousands of years and turned them into dogs.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb from {飼|か}う (to keep/raise an animal) + {慣|な}らす (to accustom). The passive form {飼|か}い{慣|な}らされた is commonly used as a modifier meaning "tamed" or "domesticated."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {動物|どうぶつ}を{飼|か}い{慣|な}らす (to tame an animal)
- {飼|か}い{慣|な}らされた{鳥|とり} (a tamed bird)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手懐|てなず}ける: to tame — emphasizes winning over trust through gentleness
- {家畜化|かちくか}する: to domesticate — more scientific/formal term
